plan.goal: Add formatDuration(ms) to src/duration.js as the inverse of parseDuration (90000 gives "1m30s"), with tests in test/duration.test.js, npm test passing, delivered as one commit on a new branch. Keep it small.
plan.doneWhen: On a new branch (not main) with exactly one commit on top of main: src/duration.js exports formatDuration; formatDuration(90000) === "1m30s"; parseDuration(formatDuration(x)) === x for a range of non-negative integers, including 0 and values with ms remainders; invalid input behaves as decided in q2; test/duration.test.js covers these; `npm test` exits 0, and a Warden reproduces that result in a fresh context.
findings: parseDuration (src/duration.js:3-10) accepts integer tokens with units ms, s, m, h and d, sums them, and throws only when no token matches.
Parsing handles integers only, with no decimals or negatives, so output that round-trips needs whole-unit tokens down to ms.
Greedy output from days down to ms, skipping zero parts, round-trips every non-negative integer ms. For example, 1500 gives "1s500ms".
0 needs an explicit token such as "0ms", because parseDuration throws on an empty string.
The package is ESM with "test": "node --test". The test file has 4 tests and imports parseDuration and clampDuration.
Git is on main with a clean working tree. The scout's scope blocked npm test, so whether the suite passes today is not yet known.
assumptions: The canonical form uses no separator, largest unit first, and skips zero parts, for example "1h2m3s".
The Smith's preset allows running npm test; if it doesn't, I'll raise a scope ask rather than skip the check.
The commit stays local; nothing is pushed or merged.
